LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Rhythm. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can a rhythm be created?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write the French rhythm taa and ta-te, names using free hand lettering
2. describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. write the French rhythm taa and ta-te, names using free hand lettering
   In simple words: practise until you can write the French rhythm taa and ta-te, names using free hand lettering. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern
   In simple words: practise until you can describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Rhythm using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Rhythm in the examples.
2. Explain Rhythm to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Rhythm.
4. Show that you can: write the French rhythm taa and ta-te, names using free hand lettering

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Rhythm using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Rhythm important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names,
2. Clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names,
3. Write letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand lettering- ascenders and descenders,
4. Practice writing the note symbols; crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests on monotone,
5. Discuss the techniques used in composing rhythmic patterns,

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. write the French rhythm taa and ta-te, names using free hand lettering
2. describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
